text:
sara_ml: Heads-up — saw a big drop in prefix-cache hit rate after yesterday's runtime merge (ATTN-KERNEL-OPT + Q8-AUTO). Production gpt-13B traffic: hit-rate went from ~91.8% -> ~57.3% within 30m of the deploy.
jon_runtime: ugh. any obvious error logs? did the keying scheme change?
kevin_sre: alert fired for increased tail latency too. 95p latency doubled on some routes. I grabbed the cache metrics for the last 2 hours.
maria_prodeng: can you paste the metrics? need to triage impact on Dedicated customers.
kevin_sre: metrics snapshot:
  - overall_prefix_cache_hit: 0.573
  - baseline_before_deploy: 0.918
  - miss_reasons: {"key_mismatch": 63%, "stale_version": 22%, "evicted": 15%}
  - affected_models: ["gpt-13B-v1", "gpt-13B-quant-q8"]
bench-bot: ran a sample workload against canary: warmup pattern shows many unique keys per prefix. suspect non-deterministic key component.
sara_ml: I ran a quick diff of the cache key generation path. After the kernel change we started attaching a kernel_signature string to the cache key so we can safely differentiate kernels. But the kernel_signature includes a float flag string that is derived from fp_fast_math heuristics and is not stable across runs (it toggles based on minor scheduler differences).
jon_runtime: that would explain key_mismatch being dominant. keys look like:
  kvcache:key=sha256(prefix+model+kernel_sig+quant_profile)
and kernel_sig example values observed:
  "k_atn_v1_fp_opt=0.0001"
  "k_atn_v1_fp_opt=0.00010000000000002"
which obviously breaks equality.
maria_prodeng: why did we add kernel_sig to the key? intent was safe routing of mixed kernels, right?
sara_ml: yes — intent was to avoid wrong-kernel replays. but we forgot to canonicalize numeric fields. also quant profile naming changed from q8-fast -> q8_auto in the model repo post-merge; some callers still use old name so stale_version misses increased too.
jon_runtime: quick mitigation options?
kevin_sre: immediate: roll the kernel_signature patch back from prod and roll forward a normalized keying fix to canary.
sara_ml: I prepared a minimal patch: normalize kernel_signature by formatting floats to 6 decimal places and collapsing aliases for quant profiles. Also add a checksum fallback key that omits kernel_sig for lookup if primary lookup misses. Patch diff snippet:
```
- key = sha256(prefix + model + kernel_sig + quant)
+ norm_sig = format_float_fields(kernel_sig, precision=6)
+ quant = normalize_quant_name(quant)
+ primary_key = sha256(prefix + model + norm_sig + quant)
+ fallback_key = sha256(prefix + model + quant)
```
jon_runtime: looks good. can we hot patch without restart? the key normalization function is non-invasive.
kevin_sre: yes we can ship as config toggle and enable on a subset of pods.
sara_ml: bench-bot results after applying normalization on canary (10% traffic): hit-rate recovered to 88.9% on canary; tail latency back near baseline for those pods.
bench-bot: detailed bench run:
  - traffic: 1000 req/s sampled
  - canary_hit_rate: 0.889
  - prod_non_canary_hit_rate: 0.572
  - avg_tokens_saved_per_req: up 3.2
jon_runtime: great. next steps to be safe:
  1) deploy normalization to 30% and enable fallback lookup for 24h
  2) run focused warmup job that replays top-10k prefixes so we don't rely solely on users to repopulate cache
  3) add unit tests ensuring kernel_sig canonicalization and quant alias map
maria_prodeng: how long before we can revert kernel patch entirely vs keep but canonicalize?
sara_ml: prefer keep canonicalized kernel_sig — having kernel identity in key gives safety for intentional kernel differences. revert only if we see other regressions. I opened a PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/PR#4213 with tests.
kevin_sre: I'll schedule the rollout window 02:00-04:00 UTC and monitor. also adding an alert for sudden drop in fallback_hit_ratio.
jon_runtime: for warmup strategy: instead of bulk replay across all nodes, let's target warmup to the smallest set of nodes (to improve hit rate quickly). idea: concentrated warmup + decreased batch size threshold for warmup traffic so those requests are prioritized.
sara_ml: added a config to mark warmup traffic with header X-RW-WARMUP and the router will preferentially route to warmup-only pool. early results show faster convergence.
bench-bot: warmup script command (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/infra/warmup \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-13B-v1","prefixes": "top_10k", "routes":"warmup-pool"}'
```
maria_prodeng: please prepare a customer note if any SLA surfaces; include timeline and root cause summary.
jon_runtime: PR for monitoring changes (add kernel_sig_cardinality, fallback_lookup_ratio, prefix_hotness) is up.
sara_ml: tl;dr: root cause = non-deterministic float formatting inside kernel_signature + quant name drift after model repo rename -> cache key mismatches -> big hit-rate regression. Fix = canonicalize kernel_sig, normalize quant names, add fallback lookup, and targeted warmup. Rolling to prod in the window kevin scheduled.
kevin_sre: monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/d/abc123/prefix-cache (watch the canary panel).
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/key-normalize-canary -> 2026-03-18T02:10:00Z
jon_runtime: postmortem TODO: add a lint check in the kernel signature generator and a checklist item for model repo renames that touch quant names.
maria_prodeng: thanks all — appreciate the quick triage. keep customer-ops looped.
sara_ml: I'll follow up with PR link and a short explainer doc in product channel.
kevin_sre: closing the incident if metrics hold after 6h on canary -> proceed to 100%.
